You are implementing one stream of a Python project: repo /Users/yashvi/orange_health_assignemnt. Your worktree must be at the tip of branch `feat/demo-build`. Run `git log --oneline -1`; if it isn't the latest feat/demo-build commit, run `git reset --hard feat/demo-build` (no local changes exist). Then `uv sync --all-extras`.

Read: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-demo-scope.md (Global Constraints, **Task 14**), docs/specs/S-A-openaq-and-schema.md §5 (tables), src/aqagent/db.py (the actual tables, the source of truth for columns), src/aqagent/repo.py (don't modify it) and src/aqagent/decide/pipeline.py (`REASON_TEXT`).

Your task is the read side of Task 14. The orchestrator is writing the runner, CLI and scheduler, so skip those.
- src/aqagent/queries.py: read-only query functions over a Connection. `list_users`, `feed(conn, user_id, replay_run=None, until=None)` (delivered notifications, newest first; `replay_run=None` means live only, i.e. decisions.replay_run IS NULL), `decisions(conn, user_id=None, start=None, end=None, outcome=None, replay_run=None)`, `explain(conn, notification_id)` (decision row, trace, the station_scores rows whose ids are in decisions.score_ids, readings as known at decisions.evaluated_at for the 24 h before period_end via `repo.readings_as_of`, the latest baselines row for that sensor with fitted_at ≤ evaluated_at, and rules_version) and `export_rows(conn, user_id, replay_run=None)`.
- src/aqagent/learn/feedback.py: `record(conn, notification_id, user_id, action: Literal["acted","dismissed","not_useful"], at) -> int`. It raises `UnknownNotification` for a missing id.
- src/aqagent/api.py: `create_app(engine, clock) -> FastAPI` with these JSON shapes, which a separate watch-demo app depends on, so match them exactly:
  - `GET /health` → `{ok: true, sensors: [{sensor_id, city, newest_reading_at, age_hours}]}` (200 even on an empty DB)
  - `GET /users` → `[{id, display_name, city, station_id, persona}]`
  - `GET /users/{id}/feed?replay_run=&until=` → newest-first `[{id, created_at, delivered_at, kind, event_kind, band, body, next_action, decision_id}]`. `event_kind` and `band` come from the notification's context_facts (keys "event_kind" and "now.band"), null if absent. `until` filters `delivered_at <= until`.
  - `GET /decisions?user_id&start&end&outcome&replay_run` → rows `{id, evaluated_at, period_end, user_id, outcome, reason_code, reason, trigger}`
  - `GET /notifications/{id}/explain` → `{decision: {outcome, reason_code, reason, evaluated_at, trigger}, trace, scores, readings, baseline, rules_version}`
  - `POST /notifications/{id}/feedback` with body `{action}` → 201 `{id}`; 404 for an unknown id; 422 for a bad action
  - `GET /users/{id}/export?replay_run=` → CSV text with header `delivered_at,kind,body,next_action,decision_id`
  Datetimes are ISO 8601 UTC strings. 404 for unknown users and notifications.
- tests/test_api.py: build an in-memory SQLite (`db.make_engine("sqlite://")`, `create_all`), insert a station, sensor, user, user_rules, station_scores, decisions (one sent with a notification, one suppressed, one held, plus one replay-tagged) and notifications directly with SQLAlchemy inserts, then use FastAPI's TestClient. Cover `test_qa_obs_03_explain`, `test_qa_obs_04_missing_nudge_query`, `test_qa_obs_05_export`, `test_qa_fb_01_feedback_recorded` (user_rules unchanged after), `test_qa_fb_02_unknown_404`, `test_health_empty_db`, `test_feed_contract_shape` (exact keys) and `test_qa_obs_06_live_excludes_replay`.

Rules: strict TDD (write a test, run it, watch it fail correctly, implement, watch it pass). Only create new files (queries.py, learn/feedback.py, api.py, tests/test_api.py); modify nothing else, and report needed changes instead. No wall-clock reads (`datetime.now` etc.) anywhere in src: use the injected clock. `uv run pytest -q` must be fully green. Commit on your worktree branch with messages ending in "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>". Do not push or merge.

Final report (≤200 words): branch, commits, test result, routes, and any deviations with what they cost if wrong.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]

If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead, an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No "@", no leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no "@" anywhere, no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

<system-reminder>
The following MCP servers require authentication before their tools can be used:
plugin:design:figma
plugin:design:intercom
plugin:engineering:asana
plugin:engineering:atlassian
plugin:engineering:datadog
plugin:engineering:github
plugin:engineering:linear
plugin:engineering:notion
plugin:engineering:pagerduty
plugin:engineering:slack
plugin:vercel:vercel

Claude cannot start the OAuth flow itself. If the user's request depends on one of these servers (even if they didn't name it explicitly), or they ask about it, tell them that it needs to be authorized — for claude.ai connectors, via their claude.ai connector settings; for other servers, via /mcp — and that the capability is unavailable until they do. Otherwise carry on with the request and do not mention these servers. Do not ask the user for authorization codes, tokens, or callback URLs.
</system-reminder>

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- compound-engineering:ce-adversarial-document-reviewer: Conditional document-review persona for high-stakes documents -- those with significant architectural decisions, new abstractions, or more than 5 requirements. Challenges premises, surfaces unstated assumptions, and stress-tests decisions rather than evaluating document quality. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- compound-engineering:ce-adversarial-reviewer: Conditional code-review persona, selected when the diff is large (>=50 changed lines) or touches high-risk domains like auth, payments, data mutations, or external APIs. Actively constructs failure scenarios to break the implementation rather than checking against known patterns. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write)

- compound-engineering:ce-agent-native-reviewer: Reviews code to ensure agent-native parity -- any action a user can take, an agent can also take. Use after adding UI features, agent tools, or system prompts. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- compound-engineering:ce-ankane-readme-writer: Creates or updates README files following Ankane-style template for Ruby gems. Use when writing gem documentation with imperative voice, concise prose, and standard section ordering. (Tools: All tools)

- compound-engineering:ce-api-contract-reviewer: Conditional code-review persona, selected when the diff touches API routes, request/response types, serialization, versioning, or exported type signatures. Reviews code for breaking contract changes. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write)

- compound-engineering:ce-architecture-strategist: Analyzes code changes from an architectural perspective for pattern compliance and design integrity. Use when reviewing PRs, adding services, or evaluating structural refactors. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- compound-engineering:ce-best-practices-researcher: Researches and synthesizes external best practices, documentation, and examples for any technology or framework. ## 1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{...}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## 470653a9-ca83-4253-8a6d-0a608e64bb1b
Vercel MCP provides over 200 tools. Capabilities:
Deployments: builds, status/logs/files, aliases, promotions, rollbacks, rolling releases and sharing/access.
Insights: runtime errors/logs, Web Analytics, observability metrics, usage/billing and agent run traces.
Configuration: projects, accounts/teams/access groups, environment variables, domains/pricing/registration, DNS/TLS, routes/redirects, microfrontends, feature flags, Blob stores and Global Config (Edge Config).
Platform: cache artifacts/invalidation, Marketplace integrations, Connect, firewall/protection, KMS, Vercel CI/checks, Sandbox sessions/commands/files/snapshots, drains, webhook inspection and account events.
Collaboration: Toolbar comments, Claude Design imports and documentation search.

Use tool input schemas. Reuse known team/project IDs and connection scope; never guess. Discover only missing scope; ask if the target remains ambiguous.

For failed deployments, inspect state and build logs. For production errors, start with get_runtime_errors, then get_runtime_logs.

Use supported project/deployment/environment/time filters. Follow pagination for complete results; report partial data. Inspect every result. Distinguish observed failures from suspected causes.

Verify changes before reporting completion. Check uncertain writes before retrying. For requires_user_action, return the dashboard URL and leave the action pending.

For access/not-found errors, verify scope and follow reported login/SSO steps.

If MCP fails or lacks an operation, use CLI fallbacks in results, tool descriptions or _meta["vercel.com/cli"]. Follow their mappings and preserve known scope; CLI credentials and defaults are separate.

Never request or print credentials, secrets or private keys. Never decrypt environment values unless requested.

## 9852f30b-ac92-44f4-9234-e65837371ae0
Use this server when the user asks about meetings, notes, transcripts, or calendar information stored in Wispr Flow. For questions that may span multiple connected sources, use the relevant sources needed to answer the request. 36	
37	def _upsert(conn: Connection, table: sa.Table, key: dict, values: dict) -> None:
38	    where = sa.and_(*(table.c[k] == v for k, v in key.items()))
39	    if conn.execute(sa.select(sa.literal(1)).select_from(table).where(where)).first():
40	        conn.execute(table.update().where(where).values(**values))
41	    else:
42	        conn.execute(table.insert().values(**key, **values))
43

45	def upsert_station(conn: Connection, *, id: int, city: str, name: str, provider: str, timezone: str,
46	                   is_reference: bool, instrument: str | None = None, lat: float | None = None,
47	                   lon: float | None = None, license: str | None = None, attribution: str | None = None,
48	                   active: bool = True) -> None:

64	# --- readings (append-only revisions) ------------------------------------------------------------
65	
66	def _latest_versions(sensor_id: int, as_of: datetime | None):
67	    """Subquery: per period_end of `sensor_id`, the max ingested_at (<= as_of when given)."""
68	    q = (sa.select(readings.c.period_end, sa.func.max(readings.c.ingested_at).label("ingested_at"))
69	         .where(readings.c.sensor_id == sensor_id))
70	    if as_of is not None:
71	        q = q.where(readings.c.ingested_at <= as_of)
72	    return q.group_by(readings.c.period_end).subquery()
73	
74	
75	def _current(conn: Connection, sensor_id: int, start: datetime, end: datetime,
76	             as_of: datetime | None) -> list[sa.Row]:
77	    latest = _latest_versions(sensor_id, as_of)
78	    q = (sa.select(readings)
79	         .join(latest, sa.and_(readings.c.period_end == latest.c.period_end,
80	                               readings.c.ingested_at == latest.c.ingested_at))
81	         .where(readings.c.sensor_id == sensor_id, readings.c.period_end >= start, readings.c.period_end <= end)
82	         .order_by(readings.c.period_end))
83	    return list(conn.execute(q))
84	
85	
86	def upsert_readings_detailed(conn: Connection, rows: list[Reading], ingested_at: datetime,
87	                             run_id: int | None) -> tuple[list[datetime], list[datetime]]:
88	    """Store `rows`; returns (new period_ends, revised period_ends), each ascending.
89	
90	    A row is written only when (sensor_id, period_end) is new, or its value or coverage changed from the
91	    latest stored version (a revision; the old version is kept). Unchanged rows are a no-op.
92	    """
93	    new: list[datetime] = []
94	    revised: list[datetime] = []
95	    by_sensor: dict[int, dict[datetime, Reading]] = {}
96	    for r in rows:
97	        by_sensor.setdefault(r.sensor_id, {})[r.period_end] = r  # later duplicates win
98	    for sensor_id, batch in by_sensor.items():
99	        ends = sorted(batch)
100	        stored = {row.period_end: row for row in _current(conn, sensor_id, ends[0], ends[-1], None)}
101	        inserts = []
102	        for end in ends:
103	            r = batch[end]
104	            prev = stored.get(end)  # aware datetimes hash by their UTC instant
105	            if prev is not None and (prev.value, prev.coverage_pct) == (r.value, r.coverage_pct):
106	                continue
107	            values = dict(sensor_id=sensor_id, period_end=r.period_end, period_start=r.period_start,
108	                          value=r.value, coverage_pct=r.coverage_pct, ingested_at=ingested_at, run_id=run_id)
109	            if prev is not None and prev.ingested_at == ingested_at:
110	                # same instant as the latest version: amend it rather than violate the primary key
111	                conn.execute(readings.update().where(
112	                    readings.c.sensor_id == sensor_id, readings.c.period_end == r.period_end,
113	                    readings.c.ingested_at == ingested_at).values(**values))
114	            else:
115	                inserts.append(values)
116	            (revised if prev is not None else new).append(end.astimezone(UTC))
117	        if inserts:
118	            conn.execute(readings.insert(), inserts)
119	    return sorted(new), sorted(revised)
120	
121	
122	def upsert_readings(conn: Connection, rows: list[Reading], ingested_at: datetime,
123	                    run_id: int | None) -> tuple[int, int]:
124	    """Store `rows` as of `ingested_at`. Returns (new, revised) counts."""
125	    new, revised = upsert_readings_detailed(conn, rows, ingested_at, run_id)
126	    return len(new), len(revised)

129	def readings_as_of(conn: Connection, sensor_id: int, start: datetime, end: datetime,

138	    q = sa.select(sa.func.max(readings.c.period_end)).where(
139	        readings.c.sensor_id == sensor_id, readings.c.ingested_at <= as_of)
140	    return conn.execute(q).scalar()

145	def save_scores(conn: Connection, scores: list[StationScore], evaluated_at: datetime,
146	                baseline_id: int | None = None) -> list[int]:
147	    """Insert one station_scores row per score (same order); returns their ids."""
148	    ids = []
149	    for s in scores:

152	            z=s.z, ewma=s.ewma, cusum=s.cusum, slope_6h=s.slope_6h, nowcast=s.nowcast,
153	            band=_band_out(s.band), typical_band=_band_out(s.typical_band), excluded=_code_out(s.excluded),
154	            gap_break=s.gap_break, evidence=s.evidence or {}))
155	        ids.append(res.inserted_primary_key[0])
156	    return ids

158	
159	def _score_window_rows(conn: Connection, sensor_id: int, end: datetime, hours: int,
160	                       as_of: datetime | None) -> list[sa.Row]:
161	    start = end - timedelta(hours=hours)
162	    sc = station_scores.c
163	    latest = sa.select(sc.period_end, sa.func.max(sc.evaluated_at).label("evaluated_at")).where(
164	        sc.sensor_id == sensor_id, sc.period_end > start, sc.period_end <= end)
165	    if as_of is not None:
166	        latest = latest.where(sc.evaluated_at <= as_of)
167	    latest = latest.group_by(sc.period_end).subquery()
168	    q = (sa.select(station_scores)
169	         .join(latest, sa.and_(sc.period_end == latest.c.period_end, sc.evaluated_at == latest.c.evaluated_at))
170	         .where(sc.sensor_id == sensor_id)
171	         .order_by(sc.period_end))

178	                        typical_band=_band_in(r.typical_band), excluded=_code_in(r.excluded),

"""The only module allowed to read wall-clock time. Everything else receives a Clock."""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from typing import Protocol


class Clock(Protocol):
    def now(self) -> datetime: ...


class SystemClock:
    def now(self) -> datetime:
        return datetime.now(timezone.utc)


class FixedClock:
    def __init__(self, t: datetime):
        if t.tzinfo is None:
            raise ValueError("FixedClock needs a timezone-aware datetime")
        self._t = t

    def now(self) -> datetime:
        return self._t

    def set(self, t: datetime) -> None:
        self._t = t

    def advance(self, delta: timedelta) -> None:
        self._t = self._t + delta

from __future__ import annotations

from aqagent.decide.pipeline import UserClockContext, UserHourContext, evaluate_check_in, evaluate_hour, evaluate_release

UTC = timezone.utc
IST = ZoneInfo("Asia/Kolkata")
HELSINKI = ZoneInfo("Europe/Helsinki")
HOUR = timedelta(hours=1)


def window(end: datetime, n=10, z=0.0, ewma=0.0, slope=0.0, band=Band.MODERATE, typical=Band.USG, nowcast=40.0):
    def col(v):
        return list(v) if isinstance(v, (list, tuple)) else [v] * n

    zs, es, ss, bs, ns = col(z), col(ewma), col(slope), col(band), col(nowcast)
    return [
        StationScore(1, end - (n - 1 - i) * HOUR, zs[i], es[i], 0.0, ss[i], ns[i], bs[i], typical)
        for i in range(n)
    ]


def climbing(end, band=Band.UNHEALTHY, typical=Band.USG, n=10):
    """A window whose last 3 hours are a confirmed climb."""
    return window(end, n=n, z=[0.5] * (n - 3) + [2.0] * 3, ewma=[0.5] * (n - 3) + [1.5] * 3, slope=0.03,
                  band=[Band.USG] * (n - 1) + [band], typical=typical, nowcast=[40.0] * (n - 1) + [80.0])


def calm(end, band=Band.MODERATE, typical=Band.USG, n=10):
    return window(end, n=n, z=0.0, ewma=0.1, slope=0.0, band=band, typical=typical, nowcast=20.0)

def hourly(start: datetime, values, sensor_id: int = 1, coverage: float = 100.0) -> list[Reading]:

"""L1: record what a user did with a notice. Recording only; nothing here changes user_rules."""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Literal, get_args

import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.engine import Connection

from aqagent.db import feedback, notifications

Action = Literal["acted", "dismissed", "not_useful"]
ACTIONS: tuple[str, ...] = get_args(Action)


class UnknownNotification(LookupError):
    """No notification with the given id (for this user)."""


def record(conn: Connection, notification_id: int, user_id: str, action: Action, at: datetime) -> int:
    """Insert a feedback row for `notification_id`; returns its id. The caller owns the transaction."""
    if action not in ACTIONS:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown feedback action {action!r}; expected one of {ACTIONS}")
    owner = conn.execute(sa.select(notifications.c.user_id)
                         .where(notifications.c.id == notification_id)).scalar()
    if owner is None or owner != user_id:
        raise UnknownNotification(f"no notification {notification_id} for user {user_id!r}")
    res = conn.execute(feedback.insert().values(notification_id=notification_id, user_id=user_id,
                                                action=action, at=at))
    return res.inserted_primary_key[0]

"""Read-only queries behind the API and CLI exports. Every function takes a Connection and returns plain dicts.

Replay isolation: `replay_run=None` means live rows only (decisions.replay_run IS NULL); a run id selects that
replay run only. Notifications inherit their decision's replay_run.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import asdict
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.engine import Connection

from aqagent import repo
from aqagent.db import baselines, decisions as decisions_t, notifications, sensors, station_scores, stations, users

EXPLAIN_READINGS_HOURS = 24  # display window for explain: the 24 hourly readings ending at the decision's hour

EXPORT_COLUMNS = ("delivered_at", "kind", "body", "next_action", "decision_id")


def _replay_filter(replay_run: str | None):
    col = decisions_t.c.replay_run
    return col.is_(None) if replay_run is None else col == replay_run


# --- users and health ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def list_users(conn: Connection) -> list[dict]:
    q = (sa.select(users.c.id, users.c.display_name, sa.func.coalesce(users.c.city, stations.c.city).label("city"),
                   users.c.station_id, users.c.persona)
         .join(stations, stations.c.id == users.c.station_id)
         .order_by(users.c.id))
    return [dict(r._mapping) for r in conn.execute(q)]


def user_exists(conn: Connection, user_id: str) -> bool:
    return conn.execute(sa.select(users.c.id).where(users.c.id == user_id)).first() is not None


def sensor_freshness(conn: Connection, now: datetime) -> list[dict]:
    """Per sensor: its city, the newest period_end known at `now`, and that reading's age in hours (None if none)."""
    q = (sa.select(sensors.c.id, stations.c.city)
         .join(stations, stations.c.id == sensors.c.station_id)
         .order_by(sensors.c.id))
    out = []
    for sensor_id, city in conn.execute(q):
        newest = repo.newest_reading_at(conn, sensor_id, now)
        age = None if newest is None else (now - newest).total_seconds() / 3600
        out.append({"sensor_id": sensor_id, "city": city, "newest_reading_at": newest, "age_hours": age})
    return out


# --- feed and export -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _facts_get(facts: dict | None, dotted: str):
    """`facts["now"]["band"]` for "now.band"; falls back to a flat "now.band" key. None when absent."""
    if not facts:
        return None
    node = facts
    for part in dotted.split("."):
        if not isinstance(node, dict) or part not in node:
            return facts.get(dotted)
        node = node[part]
    return node


def _delivered(user_id: str, replay_run: str | None, until: datetime | None = None):
    n = notifications.c
    q = (sa.select(notifications)
         .join(decisions_t, decisions_t.c.id == n.decision_id)
         .where(n.user_id == user_id, n.delivered_at.is_not(None), _replay_filter(replay_run)))
    if until is not None:
        q = q.where(n.delivered_at <= until)
    return q


def feed(conn: Connection, user_id: str, replay_run: str | None = None,
         until: datetime | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Delivered notifications for `user_id`, newest first."""
    n = notifications.c
    q = _delivered(user_id, replay_run, until).order_by(n.delivered_at.desc(), n.id.desc())
    return [{
        "id": r.id, "created_at": r.created_at, "delivered_at": r.delivered_at, "kind": r.kind,
        "event_kind": _facts_get(r.context_facts, "event_kind"), "band": _facts_get(r.context_facts, "now.band"),
        "body": r.body, "next_action": r.next_action, "decision_id": r.decision_id,
    } for r in conn.execute(q)]


def export_rows(conn: Connection, user_id: str, replay_run: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Delivered notifications for `user_id`, oldest first, with the EXPORT_COLUMNS keys."""
    n = notifications.c
    q = _delivered(user_id, replay_run).order_by(n.delivered_at, n.id)
    return [{k: getattr(r, k) for k in EXPORT_COLUMNS} for r in conn.execute(q)]


# --- decisions and explain -----------------------------------------------------------------------

def decisions(conn: Connection, user_id: str | None = None, start: datetime | None = None,
              end: datetime | None = None, outcome: str | None = None,
              replay_run: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Decision rows with start <= period_end <= end, in period_end order (then id)."""
    d = decisions_t.c
    q = sa.select(d.id, d.evaluated_at, d.period_end, d.user_id, d.outcome, d.reason_code, d.reason, d.trigger) \
        .where(_replay_filter(replay_run))
    if user_id is not None:
        q = q.where(d.user_id == user_id)
    if start is not None:
        q = q.where(d.period_end >= start)
    if end is not None:
        q = q.where(d.period_end <= end)
    if outcome is not None:
        q = q.where(d.outcome == outcome)
    return [dict(r._mapping) for r in conn.execute(q.order_by(d.period_end, d.id))]


def explain(conn: Connection, notification_id: int) -> dict | None:
    """Everything behind one notification's decision, as known when it was made. None for an unknown id."""
    d = conn.execute(sa.select(decisions_t)
                     .join(notifications, notifications.c.decision_id == decisions_t.c.id)
                     .where(notifications.c.id == notification_id)).first()
    if d is None:
        return None

    score_ids = list(d.score_ids or [])
    scores = []
    if score_ids:
        rows = conn.execute(sa.select(station_scores).where(station_scores.c.id.in_(score_ids)))
        by_id = {r.id: dict(r._mapping) for r in rows}
        scores = [by_id[i] for i in score_ids if i in by_id]

    start = d.period_end - timedelta(hours=EXPLAIN_READINGS_HOURS - 1)
    readings = [asdict(r) for r in repo.readings_as_of(conn, d.sensor_id, start, d.period_end, d.evaluated_at)]

    b = conn.execute(sa.select(baselines)
                     .where(baselines.c.sensor_id == d.sensor_id, baselines.c.fitted_at <= d.evaluated_at)
                     .order_by(baselines.c.fitted_at.desc(), baselines.c.id.desc()).limit(1)).first()

    return {
        "decision": {"outcome": d.outcome, "reason_code": d.reason_code, "reason": d.reason,
                     "evaluated_at": d.evaluated_at, "trigger": d.trigger},
        "trace": d.trace,
        "scores": scores,
        "readings": readings,
        "baseline": None if b is None else dict(b._mapping),
        "rules_version": d.rules_version,
    }

The read side of Task 14 is done and committed. The full suite passes: 193 tests, including the no-wall-clock check. I wrote the API tests first and saw them fail because the modules didn't exist yet, then implemented.

New files only: src/aqagent/queries.py, src/aqagent/learn/feedback.py, src/aqagent/api.py, tests/test_api.py. Nothing else needs changing.

Routes, all with the shapes you specified: GET /health, GET /users, GET /users/{id}/feed, GET /decisions, GET /notifications/{id}/explain, POST /notifications/{id}/feedback, GET /users/{id}/export.

Deviations and what they cost if wrong:
1. /health reads freshness from readings, not ingestion_runs as the plan says. A one-line swap if you want the plan's version.
2. /decisions with no replay_run returns live rows only, ordered oldest first by period_end. start/end filter period_end, inclusive.
3. explain returns 24 readings ending at period_end. This window is a constant in queries.py, not in params.
4. Feedback is accepted for any known notification, delivered or not, under the notification's owner.
5. Datetimes come out as "+00:00", not "Z". Query times without a timezone are read as UTC.
6. Band is read from context_facts["now"]["band"], with a flat "now.band" key as fallback.
7. I added helpers user_exists, notification_user and sensor_freshness in queries.py.
